Annual price indices, for moving money between years

Source: R/currency-data.R
currency_deflator.Rd

A deflator moves a value between points in time within one currency, which is a different question from an exchange rate and needs different data. Two bases are carried: gdp is the default, being the economy-wide numeraire and the convention the World Bank and IPCC use for constant-price comparisons; cpi is offered because published technology cost data is often deflated on that basis instead.

Usage

currency_deflator

Format

A data frame of one row per currency, basis and year:

code

ISO 4217 currency code

area

ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 code of the area the index is for

year

calendar year

basis

"gdp" or "cpi"

index

the price index, in its own base

source

the series the value came from, or "user" for a row from add_currency_deflator()

Source

World Bank World Development Indicators, series NY.GDP.DEFL.ZS (GDP deflator) and FP.CPI.TOTL (consumer price index). Licensed CC BY 4.0, https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/public-licenses.

Details

The index base year varies by series and does not matter: only the ratio of two years is ever used.

A deflator is national but a currency need not be, so area names the country the index was taken from. Where no aggregate exists for a currency union the largest member stands in – the euro is the live case, having an exchange rate of its own but no euro-area deflator in these series, so it deflates on Germany. The column is there so that substitution is visible rather than implied.

See also

currency_codes, currency_fx

Examples

subset(currency_deflator, code == "USD" & basis == "gdp" & year >= 2020)
#>       code area year basis    index         source
#> 13942  USD  USA 2020   gdp 100.0000 NY.GDP.DEFL.ZS
#> 13943  USD  USA 2021   gdp 104.5630 NY.GDP.DEFL.ZS
#> 13944  USD  USA 2022   gdp 112.0000 NY.GDP.DEFL.ZS
#> 13945  USD  USA 2023   gdp 116.1443 NY.GDP.DEFL.ZS
#> 13946  USD  USA 2024   gdp 119.0274 NY.GDP.DEFL.ZS
#> 13947  USD  USA 2025   gdp 122.3616 NY.GDP.DEFL.ZS
